Cc: tom.blake@pioneerthera.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor intake & pricing structure questions

Hi Sofia / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. As requested, attaching our standard SOW and a short vendor intake packet to get Pioneer onboarded quickly. High-level on pricing for the hosted API (this is what we typically propose for customers your scale):
- Pay-as-you-go per-token rates with commit tiers applied as blended discounts; example tiers we recommend: 
  - Up to 1M tokens/month: $0.00080/token (list)
  - 1M–5M tokens/month committed: $0.00060/token (tiered discount)
  - >5M tokens/month committed: $0.00045/token (enterprise rate)
- You can commit monthly or annually. Annual commit gets an additional 10% off the committed tiers.
- Billing can be via PO + Net terms (we typically accept Net30/Net45 for enterprise).
- Overages are billed at the list rate during the month and reconciled monthly against committed volumes; if you hit the annual commit threshold we retroactively apply the committed rate as a credit.

Two items we want to surface early because procurement calls them out often:
1) Preferred vendor forms — we're happy to complete Pioneer’s intake form but we need to check certain row-level legal asks (insurance limits, indemnity language, and data residency clauses) with our legal ops.
2) Commit expressed as tokens vs dollar minimum — we can express the commitment either as tokens/month or as a dollar minimum that converts into token credits. The conversion table is part of the SOW.

Attachments: Pioneer_Vendor_Intake_Form.pdf (blank, for you to send), Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf

Next steps: please flag the vendor form fields you need completed and any mandatory PO language (order of precedence, invoice address, PO # requirements) and I’ll coordinate with our legal and finance to get you a filled form + counterproposal on payment terms.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Thanks for the note and attachments. A couple of procurement items up front: 
- We'll need Redwood to complete our standardized Preferred Supplier Form (attached). Please fill the operational fields and confirm you accept PO as the primary contract instrument with the MSA attached as an appendix.
- Payment terms: Pioneer standard is Net60. Can Redwood accept Net60 for initial PO? If not, please propose a counter.
- We prefer commitments to be expressed as a fixed monthly dollar minimum (so our accounting system can track against a budget line). Can you convert your token tiers to a dollar-commit table?
- Overages: we need visibility on automatic true-ups and any retroactive credits. Procurement will push back if there is ambiguity on how overage credits are applied.
- Insurance and indemnity: our legal team will redline if your insurance minimums don't match our requirements.

I'll route the vendor form and a copy of our supplier terms. If Redwood cannot accept PO-first ordering or Net60 we will need to escalate.

Camila / Laura — quick internal sync before we send back the form. Notes and proposed approach: 
- We should complete Pioneer’s supplier form rather than ask them to accept our form. Sales + Legal can populate the operational fields; Legal will flag any unacceptable clauses.
- Payment terms: pivot to Net45 as a compromise. Offer Net60 for first PO for new enterprise accounts if they sign an annual commit (formalized in SOW/Order). Net60 alone without any commitment is hard for finance.
- Commit structure: offer two options in the SOW (they can pick):
  1) Token-based commit: tokens/month converted to a dollar commitment using the then-current published list price; true-up monthly, credits roll forward for 90 days.
  2) Dollar-based commit: fixed $/month for a 12-month term, where we translate that into token credits internally; overages billed at list rate and reconciled monthly; if annual dollar run rate is achieved we apply retroactive blended discount as a month-end credit.
- For procurement comfort, include a CSV price sheet and a short example calculation showing how a $50k/month commit maps to tokens and tier pricing.
- Legal asks to see the vendor form and will return a redline; we should not sign anything that creates broad indemnities without legal approval.

I can draft the populated supplier form and the price conversion table. Camila — if you want, I'll take point on the vendor form and loop legal.

Marcus
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear requests. Attached is the completed supplier intake form (we filled all operational fields and marked redlines where legal review is required). Summary of what we can commit to now: 

1) Vendor form: attached and completed; please confirm receipt. We noted three clauses for legal review: insurance limits (we provided current policy copy), broad indemnity language, and a narrow data residency clause you flagged.

2) Payment terms: we can accept Net45 as our standard counteroffer. For the first PO we are willing to accept Net60 if Pioneer signs a 12-month dollar-based commit (example: $XXXk/month).

3) Commit conversion: attached price sheet (CSV) and example calculations. Short version: a $50k/month dollar commit converts to ~62.5M generation tokens/month at the agreed committed tier (example table in CSV). Overages are billed at list rate monthly; if annualized committed volume is achieved we apply a retroactive credit to reconcile to the committed tier. Credits will show as invoice adjustments on the monthly statement.

4) Order of precedence / PO acceptance: we will accept a PO referencing our MSA/SOW. We ask that the PO include a clause that the MSA governs service-level obligations and that the PO governs quantity/pricing for that order. We added that as a limited clause in the populated supplier form.

5) Next steps: 
- Please have your legal review the vendor form redlines.
- If acceptable, route the PO referencing the attached SOW and we will countersign via DocuSign.

Attachments: Completed_Pioneer_Vendor_Intake_Form.pdf, Redwood_price_sheet.csv, Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf

Regards,
